totals.rows_scoped: whole-file origin walk (schemas/skill.schema.json's origin field wherever it occurs: contract.standards, contract.operations, contract.shapes, contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, instructions, best_practices, purpose), matching the exact recursive origins() walk tools/acceptance_check.py runs to compute T-t9-02's share for these seven cap-layer ideal facets (cap-model-access, cap-policy, cap-provenance, cap-scheduling, cap-state-persistence, cap-telemetry, cap-work-intake). definition_of_done, adapters, composes_with and entities were off limits per instruction and not touched; open_questions was in scope but every row there already carried sources and a quote in all seven skills before this ceremony, so none needed conversion.

conversion_rate: 27/94 of the proposed rows on file converted; share fell from a 31-44 percent range to 25-28 percent, under the 30 percent stick (T-t9-02) for all seven
method: Two levers in the order the task fixed. Lever 1, delete padding: every proposed row in all seven skills was read against its sibling -implement facet, cap-consumption, cap-errors and the relevant xc- skill; none was found to restate a sibling's contract, be generic engineering advice, or reword another row in the same skill, so lever 1 was not exercised (0 deletions), matching the 0-deletion precedent set by 42-sourcing-1 and 42-sourcing-2a/2b over the same layer's other facets. Lever 2, convert: the task named four standard-governed operation classes explicitly (an OTLP export, an RFC 5545 recurrence evaluation, an OPA decision call, an in-toto statement) plus CloudEvents/A2A messages, and this pass converted the contract.operations and contract.shapes rows that are the direct calls or wire shapes those standards themselves define - cap-telemetry's emit/measure operations and its CorrelationResourceAttributes shape (OTLP resource-attribute stability, X-cross-structure-012/X-cap-telemetry-006); cap-scheduling's occurrences/next_after/declare/fire operations and its ScheduleDeclaration/OccurrenceSet shapes (RFC 5545 RRULE grammar, X-cap-scheduling-002/X-entry-composition-049); cap-policy's decide operation and its DecisionRequest/Decision shapes (the OPA/Rego document-in-decision-out API, X-cross-structure-031); cap-provenance's attest/verify operations and its Attestation shape (the in-toto/DSSE envelope-statement-predicate stack and PAE signing, X-cross-structure-050/X-cap-provenance-003); cap-work-intake's accept/normalise/job_digest/admit operations and its EntryEnvelope/IntakeAcknowledgement shapes (CloudEvents source+id uniqueness and the platform's own four-entry envelope rule, X-cap-work-intake-005/T-t6-02/T-t6-03); and cap-model-access's route/submit/claim operations and its completion-request shape, sourced to the budget-ceiling and idempotency-replay facts its own inputs name (F-b4-02, F-b4-08) and to the completions standard record (X-cap-model-access-002) rather than to F-b3-03 directly, because a literal quote naming the standard collides with the product-purity check (PRODUCTS includes 'OpenAI', which the rendered Contract section may not contain outside Adapters; the chosen substring names 'the standard other providers implement' instead). cap-state-persistence's own recorded row says explicitly that no standard fixes its operations' call surface (F-b3-17: '(no standard; see B5)'), matching the task's own carve-out that genuinely-ours operations stay proposed - so its two conversions went to shapes whose specific fields are supported by kb records regardless: Head.sealed_at by F-a5-03's closing-digest-is-next-opening-digest chain property, and InclusionProof by X-cross-structure-052's third-party-verifiable Merkle log. Every quote was checked as a literal substring of a cited record before conversion; several reused a quote already carried by another row in the same skill (permitted - the compose-by-name warning is deduplicated per (skill, id, quote) triple across skills, not within one), and none introduced a new cross-skill collision beyond what already existed pre-edit (checked by diffing warning output against git HEAD for each file). Rows left proposed are the skill's own genuinely-ours design claims (an async ticket pattern, a pure routing function, a platform-owned predicate URI, a canonicalisation scheme deferred to an open question) - all but cap-state-persistence's already carry an appended 'Research query:' sentence from earlier ceremonies; cap-state-persistence's own convention instead routes its unresolved standard-citability question through its open_questions section (T-t5-02, 1-3-1), which this pass left untouched since every open_questions row there already carries sources and a quote.
quality_note: python3 tools/render_skill.py .claude/skills/<name> && python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only <name> was run after every skill: 0 errors for all seven. Warnings present after editing (cap-model-access 6, cap-policy 2, cap-provenance 2, cap-scheduling 2, cap-state-persistence 2, cap-telemetry 1, cap-work-intake 2) were checked row-by-row against the pre-edit file (git diff on the untouched rows that generate each warning) and are byte-identical in cause to the pre-ceremony state: the 'definition_of_done.criterion is not a pure shell command' warning is a repo-wide lesson-59 check over criterion text this ceremony never touched: the 'compose by name, not by copy' warnings on cap-policy/cap-scheduling/cap-work-intake fire on a quote (T-t6-02's 'All four enter through the same shape.', F-b4-07's 'Typed and machine-readable') that an untouched invariants or not_exposed row in the same skill already carried before this ceremony and that a builds_on sibling (cap-errors) also cites; reusing that same quote on a newly-converted operation or shape row does not add a new warning line because the check is deduplicated per (skill, id, quote), confirmed by re-running validate before and after each conversion. cap-model-access's five restate-and-extend (MECH-2) warnings are all on instructions/best_practices/invariants rows this ceremony did not edit. No new warning was introduced under any of the seven skills' own --only name. Tooling note: tools/validate_skills.py's check_structure() was found mid-ceremony with its warns parameter dropped from both the function signature and its call site (a concurrent edit by another agent in this multi-agent ceremony, confirmed by reproducing the identical crash on a clean git stash of this session's own changes) - it raised NameError on every skill with a criterion containing a backtick, which is most of this layer, blocking the required render-then-validate loop for all seven target skills and for the rest of the repository. Restored the dropped parameter (signature and call site) as the minimal fix; no validation logic changed. A full unscoped run after the fix and after all seven skills reports 102 skills checked, 1 error (cap-isolation, a file this ceremony does not own and never touched), 300 warnings - unrelated to this ceremony's scope.

examples.row: emit's output: the operation name is drawn from the vocabulary's own lifecycle attribute, which already spans create_agent, invoke_agent, invoke_workflow and execute_tool
examples.quote: including create_agent, invoke_agent, invoke_workflow, execute_tool, retrieval, plan, plus memory operations

examples.row: the occurrences operation set reads the RRULE grammar the standard itself defines
examples.quote: An RRULE is the recurrence rule grammar defined in RFC 5545 that describes a repeating schedule as a single string.

examples.row: decide is the standard's own document-in, decision-out shape, not an invented call
examples.quote: evaluates the input against the specified policies to return an access decision in JSON

examples.row: the Attestation envelope's signatures field signs the encoding, per the standard, never the raw JSON
examples.quote: The signature is computed over the Pre-Authentication Encoding (PAE) of the payload type and payload bytes, not over the raw JSON, which prevents format-confusion attacks.

examples.row: job_digest reads the same producer-uniqueness obligation the event standard already places on source and id
examples.quote: Producers MUST ensure that source + id is unique for each distinct event.

examples.row: Head.sealed_at: a sealed head is the opening head of the next run
examples.quote: each run's closing digest is the next run's opening digest
